research_question: If capability semantics are made explicit and correctly supervised, can the compiler learn to consume them during TaskIR construction? (Resolver trained separately in 6B-2, NOT here)

fields: selected_capabilities (GT trajectory tools; oracle-selected arms ONLY)
corpus_v4.tiers: G1 + audited G2 as strong supervision; G3 metadata excluded from conditioning blocks
corpus_v4.audit: results/phase6/corpus_v4_audit.json — ALL ASSERTIONS PASS (plan params nonempty 98.76%, selected all in available 100%, no signature >=90%, EXEC_ACTION-only signature 4.82%)

arms.C1: task + selected canonical SKILL NAMES only — tests whether Skill ISA alone guides composition
arms.C2: task + selected concrete capability + canonical skill — PRIMARY candidate
arms.C3: task + full available CapabilityIR table (selection implicit) — tests whether pushing Resolver back into Composer fails again

training: Qwen2.5-3B QLoRA r16 a32 lr1.5e-4 1 epoch batch4 accum4 seq2048; seeds 42/43/44 for C1/C2, 42 for C3; no 7B; no external benchmark data
metrics: NEW Condition Adherence: provided-skill recall/precision, hallucinated-skill rate

decision_matrix.B1_composer_conditioning_works: C2 provided-skill recall >90% + OpSeq high + EXEC_ACTION recovered -> proceed to Resolver (6B-2)
decision_matrix.B2_composer_ignores_oracle_skills: C2 provided-skill recall low -> STOP Resolver; pivot to hierarchical composition (skill skeleton -> TaskIR expansion)
decision_matrix.B3_chain_fails: individual arms work but chain fails -> interface mismatch investigation

sixb0_wording: GT-derived domain-inventory mechanism diagnostic (not clean env-visible matched-information); inventory = domain ref-name union + tools.py; prompt cap 15
